Hi Paul / Sophie — thanks for the questions. Below is the gating checklist we require for a standard hosted->dedicated migration, plus the staging timeline we recommend. I've kept this tight so your team can take it to procurement and infra.

Gating checklist (minimal) — must be green before production traffic shift:
1) Capacity validation: baseline synthetic soak at 120% of your reported peak qps for 2 hours with P95 latency <= 380ms and <0.5% error rate.
2) KV/prefix cache check: prefix cache hit rate >= 60% on representative traffic (we'll provide tracer tooling).
3) Tokenization/seq-length alignment: 99% of requests must conform to the sampled token-length profile (we use load_profile_samples.json).
4) End-to-end functional: 50 golden prompts (customer-provided) must match expected policy/format outputs; tolerance defined in the attached checklist.
5) Observability hooks: tracing and per-route token-level cost reporting enabled; no gaps in logs for the soak window.

Recommended timeline (example, 3-week runway):
- Week 0 (Coordinations): finalize PO & legal SLA (Marissa lead). HubSpot deal RDW-8237 to be updated.
- Week 1 (Staging & Load): provision dedicated pod(s); run synthetic soak and KV/cache tuning (engineering lead: Karthik).
- Week 2 (Canary Ramp): 1% -> 10% -> 25% traffic ramp over 4 days with health checks at each step.
- Week 3 (Cutover Weekend): final 75%->100% cutover on agreed weekend with rollback window and 24h post-cut monitoring.

Rollback plan (if canary/regression): automated traffic split to hosted API (same model version pinned) + immediate freeze on routing. We keep a parallel short-lived tunnel to redirect tokens to hosted until rollback is complete (typically <60 minutes).

Attachments: validation-checklist.xlsx, load_profile_samples.json.

I'll attach the checklist and can run through the validation steps with your infra team on Thursday if that works.

Thanks,
Kimberly

Thanks Marissa — legal is reviewing the SLA now. A couple more technical clarifications for your infra lead: 

- During canary, do you recommend a single dedicated pool or a mixed pool (dedicated + pinned hosted fallback)? Which gives faster rollback?
- For KV-prefix cache behavior, how invasive are the instrumentation hooks? We prefer minimal changes on our side.

Sophie and I will aim to return the signed MCP early next week.

- Paul

On Thu, Nov 5, 2026 at 09:48 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Paul / Sophie — copying my response inline so we have the plan on record.
> 
> - Recommendation for canary: provision a single dedicated pool and use traffic-splitting at the controller layer. That provides the fastest, deterministic rollback to hosted because the routing decision is external and reversible.
> - Fallback path: we keep model variants pinned and a direct route back to hosted with preserved request IDs so tracing continuity stays intact. Typical rollback time < 15 minutes if automation triggers.
> - Instrumentation: we push a lightweight tracer that samples requests and reports prefix cache stats. It is non-invasive (agentless) and reads from logs/headers; no app code change required.
> - Cutover window estimate: 4 hours for the full 100% shift including verification and buffer. We'll block a weekend window (Nov 14-15) pending PO.
> 
> I'll run the synthetic soak on our staging cluster Friday morning and post the results to the Drive link.
> 
> Cheers,
> Karthik
